picks.name: Oceanic
picks.bio: Dutch producer and Nous'klaer Audio mainstay, drawing on classic Detroit and UK techno while working in post-modern breakbeat techno. "ICI" (Aug 14, 2026 -- one day old) is a 4-track EP: two rhythmic club cuts bookending two slower, vibier tracks.
picks.why_listen: Uncluttered, groove-focused house and techno with real dancefloor architecture -- exactly the kind of functional-but-not-boring record worth grabbing the day it drops.

picks.name: upsammy
picks.source_note: Already seeded via Dekmantel; also released on Nous'klaer Audio historically, same Dutch scene as Oceanic (above).
picks.bio: Already in your seeds via the Dekmantel roster research. "Seismo" (April 10, 2026) is a collaborative album with percussionist Valentina Magaletti on PAN, born out of a commission to soundtrack an exhibition at Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum.
picks.why_listen: Mischievous vocal snippets, disorienting rhythms and collapsing sonic architectures -- a left-field, headphones-first pick rather than a club tool, good for a set that wants to unsettle for a track or two.

picks.name: Auntie Flo
picks.source_note: Already in your library ("Hey, Don't Make Trouble").
picks.bio: Brian d'Souza, already in your library, known for globally-minded house and sound-art projects. "Havana Sessions" (May 1, 2026) includes "Havana City" featuring Andrew Ashong on vocals with Cuban musicians.
picks.why_listen: A warmer, more live-instrumentation take on his usual club sound -- good if you want to work Cuban rhythm into a set without reaching for a straight cumbia or salsa record.
